claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC phase.
Cooling Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from its high-temperature BCC state produces local chemical ordering.
The local chemical ordering nucleates nanoscale B2-ordered regions.
Nanoscale B2 domains reduce the free-energy barrier for subsequent phase transformations.
B2-ordered nuclei act as energetically favorable sites for intermetallic precipitation during further annealing.
B2-ordered nuclei can promote stable oxide or spinel-like phase formation at elevated temperatures.
Local atomic diffusion at moderate undercooling causes elemental segregation and B2 ordering.
Slower cooling or prolonged annealing provides sufficient atomic mobility for ordering in either oxidizing or inert environments.
Extremely rapid quenching suppresses diffusion and compositional reordering.
A non-oxidative environment may suppress the proposed transformation pathway.
Slow-cooled and subsequently annealed samples will develop a multiphase microstructure containing B2 ordering and secondary intermetallic or oxide phases.
Rapidly quenched samples will largely retain the metastable high-temperature BCC phase with little or no local ordering.
Rapid quenching to room temperature mostly freezes the high-temperature phase without substantial secondary-phase development.
Atmosphere composition significantly alters oxidation kinetics and can alter the phase-transformation pathway.
B2-mediated transformations explain the variable phase evolution reported from a single high-temperature BCC state.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that ordering can occur during prolonged annealing in either oxidizing or inert environments, but also list a non-oxidative environment as a condition that may suppress the pathway. The distinction between B2/intermetallic evolution in inert conditions and oxide evolution in oxidizing conditions is not made consistently.
